The UI consists of four primary views 1) a top-down rendering of the scene, trajectory and 3D SDF reconstruction; 2) an augmented reality view which initially showed the 3D SDF reconstruction overlaid on the camera view using a single channel (red and transparency) colorization; 3) spectral histogram and temporal strip charts of any spectroscopic alarm outputs and count rate (only the latter is visible in Fig. 4); and 4) system control and status information. The UI has been subject to substantial updates, but the rendered content has remained fairly stable. Following the success of the original LAMP system, DTRA-NTD further supported LBNL to create a LAMP with a similar detector layout, but using Cs LiLa(BrCl) :Ce (CLLBC) detectors 2 6 with 6Li enrichment that allows for efficient thermal neutron detection while concurrently being a capable gamma-ray detector [24]. This neutron- and gamma-capable LAMP system was named NG-LAMP and proved the applicability of SDF for thermal neutrons. Concurrent to NGLAMP development, the portable radiation imaging, spectroscopy, and mapping (PRISM) and miniPRISM projects were also started with DTRA support. The former leveraged a spherical shell of co-planar grid (CPG)-readout CdZnTe(CZT) detector modules developed through the high-efficiency multi-mode imager (HEMI) [21] project, to create a dual- modality imager capable of both Compton imaging and - due to the pattern of the spherical CZT array - also capable of coded mask imaging [25]. MiniPRISM leveraged the detector technology of PRISM but did so in a LAMP package that could be flown on small unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). The MiniPRISM approach demonstrated the benefit of performing gamma-ray imaging (versus ‘proximity imaging’) in some SDF applications [26], [8]. The relative strengths of different imaging modalities will be discussed further below in Sec. 2.3.3. Many applications focus on the use of commercially available detector systems, and with NA- 241 support, in 2019 LBNL demonstrated that an H3D Polaris [27] CZT-based imager could be coupled with SDF technology to enable free-moving gamma-ray imaging [28, 29] as could a PhDs GeGIsystem[10].
